text: The year was 1889, and the last natural forest on Earth was a spectacle that many traveled miles to behold. Eli, a young botanist, stood in awe among the ancient trees, a leather-bound journal in hand as he recorded notes about species that had become legends. This sacred grove, unbeknownst to him, was about to become the centerpiece of a historic preservation effort that would challenge the technological metropolis encroaching upon the natural world. The city of Paris, known for the Eiffel Tower, was rapidly industrializing, its iron and steam threatening to swallow the remaining wild spaces. Eli’s sketches of the ancient oaks and ferns were not just scientific records; they were acts of defiance against the soot and noise of the modern age, preserving the memory of a green world that was vanishing under the shadow of progress.
